newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: ALPINE SKIING-SEIZINGER WANTS OVERALL WORLD CUP LEAD.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-SEIZINGER WANTS OVERALL WORLD CUP LEAD.

text.p: Germany's Katja Seizinger, who favours fast events, has two downhills and a super-G this weekend to help her snatch the overall World Cup lead from Sweden's Pernilla Wiberg.

Defending overall title-holder Seizinger is convinced she is 155 points behind Wiberg in the standings because there have been fewer races in the speed disciplines than in the technical ones so far this season.
But Seizinger, the 1993 super-G world and 1994 Olympic downhill champion, will have to deliver outstanding performances in order to leapfrog Wiberg.
Wiberg's showings in all races this winter have been remarkable and she has proved she is capable of podium positions in such different events as slalom and downhill.
The 26-year-old Swede surprised her competitors this winter by winning two slaloms in Semmering and Maribor as well as a super-G in Lake Louise. She was on the rostrum a further four times.
"Wiberg is in incredible form. The amazing thing is that she has been good in both the technical and the speed events this season. This is scary," said Seizinger's German coach Rainer Mutschler.

However, on Monday in Maribor, Seizinger demonstrated her willingness to put up a fight for the coveted title by clocking a third quickest second run to take overall ninth place in her weakest discipline, the slalom.
Although the German was so strong in her first slalom appearance of the season, she has opted not to put in extra slalom training hours.
"I prefer to do well in downhill and super-G than finish 20th in slalom. Although if I can always manage a result like in Maribor then that's fine by me," she said.

Seizinger will also be looking to level with Wiberg in number of season victories this weekend. The German won the opening race in Soelden and again at a downhill in Lake Louise and has stood on the podium on three other occasions.
Tough competition could come from Austrian Renate Goetschl and Italian Isolde Kostner.

Goetschl captured the Austrian women's team only victory of the winter by taking the downhill in Vail. Kostner, the reigning super-G world champion, has only managed two third places in downhill and super-G.
Austria's most consistent skier of the winter, Anita Wachter, opted to give both downhills a miss and will instead concentrate her efforts on Sunday's super-G.

Wachter, the 1993 overall World Cup title-holder is suffering from knee ligament pains. Her performances in downhill this winter were disappointing with 22nd and 18th places. She will probably also miss the downhill in Cortina D'Ampezzo on January 24.
Races in Bad Kleinkirchheim could be jeopardized by warm weather, which on Wednesday led to the cancelllation of the first downhill training and delayed a practice run on Thursday by two hours.
International Ski Federation officials and organisers at the Austrian resort are mending the softened 3,010 metres long Strohsack piste, with the chemicals used to harden snow.
